title: Terminology - Chapter 3
notes: Bill of Materials: A comprehensive list of raw materials, components and assemblies required to build or manufacture a product.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
Billing Rate: The labor rate charged to a customer which includes both cost and profit components.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
Cost Driver: A factor that can cause a change in the cost of an activity.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
Cost-Plus Pricing: A costing approach where the price of a product is set at the cost of production plus a certain profit margin.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
Job Cost Record: A written or electronic document that shows the cost of direct material, direct labor and manufacturing overhead assigned to a particular product or batch of products.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf

Job Costing: A system used for assigning costs to products or services that differ in the amount of materials, labor and overhead required. Typically used by manufacturers that produce unique or custom-ordered products in small batches.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
Labor Time Record: A written or electronic record of the time a particular direct laborer spends on each job.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf

Materials Requisition: A detailed source document that specifies the type and quantity of materials that are to be drawn from the storeroom and identifies the job to which the costs of materials are to be charged.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
Overallocated Manufacturing Overhead: The amount of overhead applied to jobs exceeds the actual manufacturing overhead costs incurred; results in jobs being overcosted.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf

Predetermined Manufacturing Overhead Rate: The rate used to apply manufacturing overhead to individual jobs; calculated before the period begins; calculated by dividing estimated total manufacturing overhead costs by the estimated total amount of cost driver or activity base. Common activity bases used in the calculation include direct labor costs, direct labor hours, or machine hours.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
Process Costing: The process of allocating costs to products by averaging costs over large numbers of identical products that pass through a series of uniform production steps.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
Production Schedule: An electronic or written document that identifies the types and quantities of products that will be produced in a particular period.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf

Purchase Order: A purchase order is a document sent to a supplier or vendor, authorizing shipment of a product to the customer at a specified price and terms. The creation of a purchase order creates a legally binding contract which cannot be changed without the consent of both parties.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf

Raw Materials Record: A written or electronic document listing the type, quantity and cost of all raw materials units received, used in production and currently in stock. A separate record is maintained for each type of raw material kept in stock.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf

Receiving Report: A written or electronic document used to report the type and quantity of items received in an incoming shipment. A 'blind' receiving report does not pre-list the type or quantities of items expected in a particular shipment. This is done to force the receiving department to identify, count and document everything received (instead of simply checking-off items/quantities that appear on a form without performing an actual item count).
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
Stock Inventory: Items normally kept on-hand to allow a company to quickly fulfill customer orders.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf

Subsidiary Ledger: A subsidiary ledger is a group of similar accounts whose combined balances equal the balance in a specific general ledger account. The general ledger account that summarizes a subsidiary ledger's account balances is called a control account or master account.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
Underallocated Manufacturing Overhead: The amount of manufacturing overhead applied to jobs is less than the amount of manufacturing overhead actually incurred; results in jobs being undercosted.
Chapter 3 Key Terms.pdf
